name: next-js-app-slides

scripts._comment_verify: Next 16 dropped the `eslint` config key, so `next build` does NOT run lint. This chain is what enforces CLAUDE.md §5 boundaries — use it in CI, not `next build` alone.
scripts.verify: npm run lint && npm run typecheck && npm run test
scripts._comment_lintreport: Same rules as `lint`, one line per problem — ESLint's stylish output prints ~15 lines of rationale per React-rule violation, which is unreadable when triaging several files.
scripts._comment_bundle: §12/§0.5: prove no server-only code reached the CLIENT bundle. Needs a `next build` first. `--self-test` runs the same needles against the SERVER bundle, where these libraries DO live, so a pass cannot be the result of patterns that match nothing.
scripts.verify:pptx:probes: tsx scripts/verify-pptx-probe2.ts && tsx scripts/verify-pptx-probe3.ts && tsx scripts/verify-pptx-probe4.ts && tsx scripts/verify-pptx-probe5.ts && tsx scripts/verify-pptx-paragraphs.ts && tsx scripts/verify-pptx-numbering.ts
scripts.verify:pptx:all: npm run verify:fixtures && npm run verify:pptx && npm run verify:pptx:assert && npm run verify:pptx:letterbox && npm run verify:pptx:thirdparty && npm run verify:pptx:probes
scripts._comment_fixture: §2 step 13's manual gate. Unlike the opentest spike, this drives the REAL container + PptxExporter, so the bytes a human opens are the bytes a user downloads.
scripts.verify:pptx:fixture:render: npm run verify:pptx:fixture && tsx scripts/render-pptx.ts out/FIXTURE-TOKEN.pptx out/render/fixture-token && tsx scripts/render-pptx.ts out/FIXTURE-TEMPLATED.pptx out/render/fixture-templated
scripts.verify:render:all: npm run verify:pptx:opentest && npm run verify:pptx:render && npm run verify:fonts && npm run verify:bullets
scripts._comment_smoke: CLAUDE.md §11 + §2's checkpoint-after-15. Needs a RUNNING server and live Bedrock credentials, which is why it is not part of `verify`. Start the server yourself (npm run dev) and run `npm run smoke`.

_comment_devDependencies: STRICTLY build/test/spike-time. The test is mechanical: if any file reachable from `lib/container.ts` imports it at the TOP LEVEL, it belongs in `dependencies` — every route imports the container, so `npm ci --omit=dev` would fail at module load, in production only. `@napi-rs/canvas`, `officeparser`, and `pdfjs-dist` are imported by `scripts/**` alone (the §1.1 render/font-substitution harnesses); tailwindcss/postcss are consumed by `next build` and inlined into the output.
_comment_dependencies:
Server-side runtime packages are here for one reason each, all of the same shape — reachable from `lib/container.ts`, so absent in a `--omit=dev` install they crash the first request rather than a build:
 • @aws-sdk/client-bedrock-runtime — `lib/repositories/factory.ts` constructs `BedrockRuntimeClient` at the top level (`@aws-sdk/client-bedrock` stays dev: only the model-listing spike uses it).
 • pptxgenjs — `lib/export/pptx-exporter.ts` imports it statically; the factory constructs `PptxExporter`. PINNED EXACT: §1.1's five constraints (C1–C5) were verified against 4.0.1 specifically, and a silent minor bump could change paragraph/bullet behaviour the exporter is written around.
 • sharp — `lib/adapters/sharp-image-luminance.ts`, reached the same way. Declared directly rather than relied on transitively through next: it is already in the tree as next's image dependency, but a minor next upgrade that dropped or renamed it would break brand uploads in production only. Ranged to match the version next resolves so npm dedupes to one copy of the native binary.
None of the three may reach the CLIENT bundle (§0.5/§12) — that is enforced separately by the ESLint boundaries and the bundle grep, not by this placement.
